messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Paging @oncall — multiple warmup failures observed for model-prod-a in us-west-2 (root thread 1867504321). Errors: OOM during load, deserialization errors, and occasional CUDA init failures. Metrics spike at 07:12 UTC. Please triage.
devon: I’m on it. seeing repeated `OOM when allocating buffer` from warmup worker on node gpu-12. logs: `std::bad_alloc` then `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY` followed by container exit code 137.
maria: Confirmed. Also a handful of `deserialize: unsupported tensor dtype` errors from the model archive extractor — looks like a corrupted shard on s3 for version v3.2.1-warmup.
jonathan: Noting pattern: failures start right after our rolling warmup rollout at 07:08 (we pushed config to prefetch larger KV cache). Could be combined effect (bigger prefetch + corrupted shard = OOM).
lia: Quick customer impact: 3 active customers on dedicated pools hit increased latency and ~12% failed requests to /v1/generate for ~10m. CS notified for affected orgs: AcmeHealth, TradeCraft, Bluebox.ai
devon: Action plan (short):
1) Abort warmup rollout immediately (rollback warmup config) — done via deploy-bot.
2) Remove corrupted shard from rotation and force re-download of model artifacts on nodes that failed (s3 rm && download)
3) Evict large non-critical models from gpu-12 pool to free memory
4) Temporarily route traffic to fallback variant model-prod-a-quantized
maria: Running command to force redownload on gpu-12 (running now):
```
kubectl exec -n runtime warmup-gpu-12 -- /bin/bash -lc 'rm -rf /var/models/model-prod-a/v3.2.1 && curl -fSL $S3_URL/model-prod-a/v3.2.1.tar.gz | tar xz -C /var/models/model-prod-a'
```
Will monitor integrity checksums after.
jonathan: I see repeated `cuBLAS: CUBLAS_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR` on gpu-15 shortly after container restart — suspect driver jitter. ops, checking node kernel logs for GPU resets.
sre-rotations: Noted node-flap history for gpu-15 earlier this week. I’ll cordon it and drain to avoid further warmup noise: `kubectl cordon gpu-15 && kubectl drain gpu-15 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`.
devon: Traffic routing executed: redirecting new warmup jobs to quantized fallback and reducing parallelism from 8 -> 2. This should reduce peak memory usage.
oncall-bot: deploy-bot: warmup-rollout: rollback triggered by devon at 07:15 UTC (reason: OOM + deserialization). Canary flags disabled.
maria: After redownload, checksum mismatch on shard-4 — confirming corrupted object in S3. I’ll mark it for reupload from build artifacts and create ticket to investigate upstream packaging.
lia: I’ll own the customer comms thread. Posting to affected customers now and opening a support incident with priority-high. ETA for full recovery estimate: 45-90 mins depending on artifact reupload and node cycling.
jonathan: For tracking: kernel logs show `NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus` on gpu-15 at 07:11:23 — likely hardware or driver OOM. I recommend we remove gpu-15 from autoscaling pool and file hardware ticket with cloud provider.
sre-rotations: gpu-15 cordoned. Scheduling replacement node and ensuring driver update applied to pool image.
devon: Temp mitigation: disabled compile-cache on warmup pods to avoid additional memory pressure from JIT/compilation caches (`COMPILE_CACHE=false`). Will monitor throughput.
maria: Reupload of shard-4 completed from artifact store at 07:34 UTC. Verified checksums matching. Triggering warmup rerun on a single node to validate.
oncall-bot: incident-bot: incident created — ID INC-1867504321. Postmortem owner: TBD. Link: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/1867504321
lia: Handoff — I’m taking the next shift (lia). Current state summary:
- Warmup rollout rolled back.
- Corrupted shard replaced and verified.
- gpu-15 cordoned; replacement requested.
- Fallback variant handling live; compile-cache disabled.
- Customer comms in flight (CS notified).
Next steps for followup: run a controlled warmup on a non-prod pool, re-enable compile-cache gradually, run artifact packaging audit, and schedule postmortem. Leaving logs and commands in #eng-runtime.
devon: Thanks team. I’ll monitor for 30m and follow up on the postmortem prep. :thumbsup:
lia: If anyone has outstanding notes, drop them now. Otherwise I’ll create the postmortem stub and assign owners. :spiral_notepad:
oncall-bot: Reminder: if symptoms reappear, escalate to SRE lead and add `priority:sev2` tag to the incident.
